name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: A motor-driven vehicle capable of cross-country travel over natural terrain without a road, such as a dirt bike or ATV; any vehicle the BMV registers for the road is excluded. An electric dirt bike or e-moto that isn't registered as a motorcycle or motor driven cycle is an off-road vehicle. Defined by Indiana Code §14-8-2-185 and regulated by IC 14-16-1 and IC 9-18.1-14.
restrictions: Capable of cross-country travel without a road, powered by anything other than muscle or wind; no limit on motor power or speed
Not an electric bicycle, which is exempt from off-road vehicle rules
Registered with the BMV for $30 every three years, with two decals on its forward half and the registration certificate carried while riding; it must have a manufacturer's identification number
Titled with the BMV if bought after December 31, 2009

Not allowed on public roads or parking lots, except to cross a non-limited-access highway at a right angle after stopping, on a road's right-of-way away from the traveled lanes, or on county roads a county or local ordinance opens to them
A driver's license is needed wherever it's ridden on a public highway
Riders under 14 need the immediate supervision of someone 18 or older, except on land they or their parent own or control
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet
A headlight and taillight from sunset to sunrise, and adequate brakes
Ridden on public land only with the managing agency's consent, and on private land only with the owner's

DNR's riding areas are Redbird and Interlake State Recreation Areas, which need a trail pass per vehicle; at Redbird every rider wears a DOT helmet and dirt bike riders under 16 must be directly supervised by a parent or guardian, and out-of-state riders may buy a $20 annual permit instead of registering
